links.outcome: Agreement and deviation of AI pipeline scores vs treating physicians and other LLM configurations against expert ground truth
links.effect: Pipeline mean Krippendorff's α 0.78 vs 0.32 standalone LLMs, 0.39 RAG, 0.31 treating physicians; mean RMSE 0.89 vs 5.81, 1.85, 1.34.
links.quote: Pipeline-generated scores showed substantially higher agreement with expert adjudication than standalone LLMs, LLMs with RAG, and treating physicians (mean Krippendorff's α: 0.78 vs. 0.32 vs. 0.39 vs. 0.31) and lower deviation from ground truth (mean RMSE: 0.89 vs. 5.81 vs. 1.85 vs. 1.34).

unlisted_practices: Separating LLM-based data extraction from deterministic score computation to reduce calculation errors and hallucinations
Expert-curated knowledge injection into LLM pipeline

screen.reason: The study empirically tests specific implementation architectures (standalone LLM vs. RAG vs. pipeline with deterministic calculation guardrail) on clinical records for risk score extraction.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation and deterministic calculation pipelines vs standalone LLM
